newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesian rupiah declines on liquidity, fixing.
newsitem.headline: Indonesian rupiah declines on liquidity, fixing.

text.p: The Indonesian rupiah declined against the dollar in hectic trading on Wednesday as tight liquidity conditions suddenly eased in the afternoon, coupled with a surprise fixing by the central bank, dealers said.
They said a sudden loosening of rupiah liquidity, with overnight money falling to 8.0/9.0 percent from the day's high of 22.0 percent, helped the dollar rebound.

Meanwhile, Bank Indonesia raised its intervention band by two points to 2,394/2,586 and the conversion band also by two points to 2,394/2,442. Spot rupiah was at 2,401.75/02.25 at 0845 GMT off a high of 2,397.5 earlier. It opened at 2,398.00/98.25.
Dealers said the dollar broke through the 2,400 resistance level after the fall of overnight money.
"It's quite an active afternoon on the back of the volatile liquidity condition. The surprise fixing seems to have lifted the dollar," one U.S. bank dealer said.
Tomorrow and today rupiah closed at 2,400.00/00.75 and 2,396.50/97.00, respectively.
Overnight swaps were at 0.5/0.7 and tom/next at 1.7/1.8.
One Japanese bank dealer said there were some arbitrage opportunities if operators had sufficient dollars because of the difference between the swap and money market rates.
"But I don't think many people would do arbitrage at fiscal year-end. Liquidity can turn around quickly," he said. "But many would borrow rupiah through the swap market."
The dealer said tom/next swaps of 1.7/1.8 points were equivalent to around 12 percent, compared with 14 percent being traded in the money market for tom/next money.
The U.S. bank dealer said operators were seen starting dollar buying as liquidity turned around.
"But the real breakthrough was when the central bank raised the fixing by two points. We saw many Singapore players come in to buy dollars," the dealer said.
Dealers said, however, there was no guarantee that liquidity would continue to be ample on Thursday.

Thursday offers the last chance for banks to settle their outstanding taxes before heading for a long weekend. The market will be closed on Friday for a public holiday and Monday for the fiscal year-end and reopen on April 1.
Swap rates also eased across the board on ample liquidity.
One-month swaps edged down to 9.5/10.5 from 10.25/11.25, two to 21.5/23.0 from 22.75/23.75, three to 32.4/34.0 from 33.50/34.25 and six to 67.0/68.0 from 68.25/69.25 points.
